title: Phased exposure contracts and observation checklist
body:
Purpose:
This is a working sketch for a cross-functional 'exposure contract' pattern and an observation checklist that product, SRE, data, and legal/CS teams can sign off on before any phased/canary/A-B exposure. The goal is to move beyond ad-hoc canaries into repeatable contracts that make responsibilities, signals, and automatic fallback behavior explicit.

Scope: 
- Applies to feature rollouts that change inference behavior (model variants, reranking, safety filters, prompt templating) or routing policies.
- Intended for staged exposure (microcanary -> ramp -> global) and A/B tests where traffic/latency/cost tradeoffs exist.
- Not intended for pure UI copy tweaks or server-side config flags with no ML impact.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Define the exposure contract: stakeholders, exposure schedule, budget (cost+latency), and must-pass telemetry signals.
- Create an observation checklist mapped to concrete dashboards/alerts and synthetic probes.
- Agree on automatic gating rules and human escalation flow in advance.
- Capture the contract as a short artifact (1 page) attached to the rollout ticket and to the release channel.

Roles & responsibilities (contract form):
- Product (owner): hypothesis, target cohorts, acceptance criteria, user-facing comms.
- Observability / SRE: instrument metrics, configure feature-level alerts, synthetic probes.
- Data/Experimentation: statistical power and analysis plan, metric calculations and SNR expectations.
- ML/Serving (serving-runtime): capacity plan, cost guardrails, fallback model definitions.
- Legal/Privacy/CS (if applicable): data handling constraints, opt-out behavior, customer comms.

Minimum content of an exposure contract (one-paragraph + bullets):
- Hypothesis and user impact (1 sentence).
- Exposure schedule (percentages and windows). Example: 0.5% -> 2% (30m) -> 10% (2h) -> 50% (24h) -> 100% (48h).
- Key metric set with exact queries (engines will attach dashboards):
  - Safety metrics: failure rate, unsafe output counts, high-severity incidents.
  - Correctness/quality: NPS-proxy, rerank CTR lift, generation BLEU-like score (where applicable).
  - Performance: p95 latency, tail inference time, token/sec throughput.
  - Cost: per-request token cost, GPU-hours delta.
  - Infra health: queue length, memory pressure, OOMs, KV-cache hit rate.
- Accept/reject thresholds: exact numeric boundaries and measurement windows.
- Fallback behavior: which model/version to route to and whether to fail open/closed.
- Observers/contacts + on-call schedule.

Observability checklist (concrete items to verify before first exposure):
- Dashboards: link to _feature_ dashboard with the above metric widgets (safety, quality, perf, cost, infra).
- Alerts: at least 3 alert categories to be present and sanity-checked: 
  1) Kill-switch alert: e.g., p95 latency > X for Y minutes OR error rate > Z -> immediate rollback.
  2) Degradation alert: quality metric drop beyond statistical threshold over sliding window.
  3) Cost spike alert: per-request cost increases beyond budget.
- Synthetic probes: create 2–4 probes that mimic heavy-usage paths and edge cases (long context, regen, stop-token edge). Probes must run pre-exposure and during each ramp step.
- Sampling plan: define how production traffic is sampled for metric computation (every Nth request vs. deterministic hashing).
- Tracing: end-to-end traces including model invocation, kernel selection, batches, and routing decision.
- Logs: structured logs with feature flag, model_version, cohort_id, route, and latency_ms.
- Eval harness: attach a small eval set (50–200 examples) run after each ramp step focusing on behavioral regressions.

Automatic gating & adaptation rules (examples):
- Immediate rollback (automated): any Kill-switch trigger -> instant route to fallback; page on-call.
- Pause ramp (automated): quality metric drop > 5% vs baseline for 30m -> pause at current exposure and notify stakeholders.
- Adaptive fallback (semi-automated): if latency or queue builds but quality is intact, reduce batch size or route a percentage to cheaper variant. Requires SRE+ML approval to enable.
- Soft rollback (manual): after automated actions, product decides to fully revert or iterate and re-launch.

Ceremony & comms (practical template):
- Pre-launch: publish exposure contract in ticket, ping #rollouts with 2-hour notice, include dashboards and synthetic probe results.
- Kick-off: 15-minute sync with stakeholders (product, SRE, ML, data) at T=0.
- Ramp checkpoints: at each scheduled ramp point, on-call runs checklist and posts summary in rollout thread.
- Post-mortem: if any threshold breached, start incident IR flow. Otherwise a 72-hour post-launch recap with metric drift notes.

Failure modes we should explicitly think about (lab notes):
- Silent quality drift (no dramatic metric but slow user satisfaction loss) -> need user-feedback channel sampling and qualitative checks.
- Telemetry blind spots: missing metrics at higher percent exposures when sampling dropped. Add adaptive sampling.
- Cost fog: spike small relative to baseline but multiplied at scale -> include cumulative spend cap and soft-limit alerts.
- Canary contamination in A/B: cohort bleed due to cookie churn or multi-device users; use deterministic hashing and reconcile with identity signals.

Lightweight template to attach to every rollout ticket (copyable):
- Hypothesis:
- Exposure schedule (explicit %s + windows):
- Primary metric (exact query):
- Kill-switch conditions (exact numbers):
- Fallback route/version:
- Synthetic probes (names + query ids):
- Observers + pager:

Open questions / TODOs (for this working doc):
- What standard lookback window should we use for quality baselining across different models? 1h/6h/24h? (ask Data team).
- Should cost guardrails be measured per-customer or global for multi-tenant customers? (ask Finance).
- Build a small UI in Console to auto-generate the one-line exposure contract — product-design backlog.
- Formal SLA for Dedicated customers when we trigger automatic rollbacks (contract language).

Next steps (near term):
- Get buy-in from SRE and Data on the minimal alert set (owner: Liam). Due: 2026-02-28.
- Prototype a synthetic-probe job template that can be checked into infra repo (owner: Diego). Due: 2026-03-10.
- Trial this contract on two upcoming rollouts (one Hosted API model swap, one rerank experiment) and capture learnings. (owner: Maya).

Notes to self: keep the initial contract intentionally small. The danger is over-engineering the gate and slowing down experiments. Focus on the 4 signals: safety, quality, perf, cost. Also keep comms lightweight (single rollout-thread + short synchs).

References & helpful links:
- Playbook: staged-deployment-signal-runbook (attached).
- Internal convo: slack thread (link in linked_artifacts).
- Related experiment template: github:pull/4821

----
Working draft — comments welcome. If you’re added as collaborator above, please annotate the rollout template in the ticket rather than editing this doc directly (helps us keep a canonical short artifact per rollout).
